title: Midnight Café
subtitle: Open only to those who haunt the hidden edges of night.

trails.title: Witness Report
trails.description: An unremarkable witness report. All rumors, whispers, and tales—every passerby keeps a few in their pockets.

content.text: A hotel security guard says he often hears a woman's sorrowful voice during his nightly rounds. But whenever he investigates, he finds no trace of anyone hiding in the hallways or rooms.

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: All things carry energy, and we are much more perceptive to it than we think.

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: Now, I would ask that you concentrate on the subtle changes around you. You will sense it; you simply need to feel.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Yes, I'll try.

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: Tell me, Adèle, which of these crystals draws you the most?
Adèle stares at the tray, rows of crystals lined up neatly, dazzling to the eye.
After a few steady breaths, she reaches toward the third crystal from the end of the second row.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Maybe this one.
A tea-brown crystal—mysterious, sacred, its smoke frozen within.

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: A smoky quartz from Brazil. Very good.

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: This crystal turns negative energy positive. It is a peace-bringer—a banisher of the dangers that trouble one's soul.

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: Now, close your eyes.

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: Seven   doubles,   seven   gates—seven   in   all   reveal   the   Sephirot.

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: Keep your breath steady and look into the darkness—search for the light.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: I see it. Only a soft glow. But it's there.

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: Take it.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: How? Do I make it come to me, or should I go towards it? I—
Her consciousness sinks, or folds inward.
Everything flows through her mind, pours back into her body, then bursts outward again.
Adèle? Come on, wake up!

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Mm ...
Wake up! Good heavens, how do you live like this!

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Huh?
She stands, holding her head. The figure before her reaches out and flicks her forehead in anger.

items.speaker: Félicienne
items.text: "Huh?" "Good morning," I think you meant to say. I've been looking all over for you, and here you are napping like a pampered cat!

items.speaker: Félicienne
items.text: You certainly know how to enjoy yourself, don't you? Abandoning me to take a doze in this cushy parlor.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Félicienne?! Where were you? I was waiting in the street for hours! You never turned up, so I had to—

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Where's Madame Bouanich? Beryl ... She ...
Words tumble on her tongue but refuse to form a sentence.

items.speaker: Félicienne
items.text: Still dreaming? Look around you. The parlor's already closed.
Adèle scans the room. They're the only ones there.

items.speaker: Félicienne
items.text: You'd likely have woken up behind bars for trespassing if I hadn't come to collect you.

items.speaker: Félicienne
items.text: What a shame! This place seems more tedious than I thought. Come on, get up. We still have time to look elsewhere.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Oh. Of course. I'll fetch the car. It's by the back door.

items.speaker: Félicienne
items.text: No, not the car. I'd rather not get into that deathtrap for a while.
Félicienne walks straight through the corridor, pushes open the main door, and takes Adèle back into the street.
The night is pitch black and silent. The wide square and ever-lively riverbank are strangely deserted.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: The street's totally empty. Where is everyone? Is there a curfew that I didn't know of?

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: The street lamps are off. Huh, I don't even see lights on in any windows.

items.speaker: Félicienne
items.text: What is wrong with you? Heaven's sake, it's a good thing I didn't let you behind the wheel.

items.speaker: Félicienne
items.text: Look. Is that not a light right over there?
A bright café glows amid the empty darkness. Clusters of flowers hang around its name so thick they almost swallow the sign.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Is that Café de Flore?

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Do they really stay open so late? Hmm. I suppose I've never checked.

items.speaker: Félicienne
items.text: I'm starving. Go see if they have any food. I'll wait outside.
She nudges Adèle forward. The glass door swings open, and bright light spills out into the street.
Café de Flore, Paris
Even this late, the café is near to bursting with life.
Adèle walks toward the counter, wondering who these patrons might be—some left-bank art group, or theater folk fresh from rehearsal ...

items.speaker: Customer?
items.text: As I was saying, Georges Bataille is looking for executioners for his secret society.

items.speaker: Customer?
items.text: Executioners—that's right! Every one of the members would rather be sacrificed in the ritual than be the one to swing the axe.

items.speaker: Customer?
items.text: Ha! Who would have thought? The norm breakers can't even bring themselves to commit violence. Is it a mercy or just selfish martyrdom?

items.speaker: Customer?
items.text: Did you see the last performance at the Théâtre du Grand-Guignol? Jack Jouvin has been the worst director I've ever seen.

items.speaker: Customer?
items.text: He ruined all the gory scenes with his so-called theatrics. What a self-absorbed man! It's hardly a theater anymore—more like a circus.

items.speaker: Customer?
items.text: I wanted to gasp at the sight of shattered bones and slit throats, not from sheer disappointment! Honestly, I miss dear Paula Maxa. Every death she brought to the stage was impeccable.

items.speaker: Customer?
items.text: Miss, I must confess I'm confused. You're saying that something will just pop into existence if everyone believes it exists?

items.speaker: Customer?
items.text: In a manner of speaking, yes. According to the studies we've been conducting, the answer may be hidden in our collective imagination.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Célia!
The name cuts through the air like a blade, slicing the animated canvas around them apart.
Every sound in the hall vanishes, leaving only the scrape of her heels retreating against the floor.
All the customers turn toward her in unison, motionless, eyes locked on the intruder.

items.speaker: Célia
items.text: Adèle? What a surprise! I thought you had no interest in my studies.
Her friend slinks over to her. Adèle holds a dumbfounded stare, completely unsure of what she's seeing.
She fixes on the darkness writhing behind Célia's back. The outlines of the customers melt away, replaced by fangs and ... fur.

items.speaker: Célia
items.text: You look pale. Come, sit with us, and have a bite to eat. It won't take long.

items.speaker: Célia
items.text: Ah!
Adèle grabs her friend's wrist, yanking her close as they sprint for the glass door behind them.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: We need to go, Célia!

items.speaker: Célia
items.text: You're hurting me. What's going on? Adèle? Ah!
She glances back.
Their faces are no longer recognizable. Mounds of dark flesh melt into a filthy, oozing slurry that drips into the surrounding dark.
What's left of their human parts peels away, and a ghostly fire drifts upward around them.
*roar*
*bang*

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Damn it, the car—it's still in the alley! Célia, stay close!

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Félicienne! Run!
When she bursts through the door, the streets are empty. Adèle finds herself actually hoping that Félicienne stuck to her stubborn ways and she's already long gone.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Go on ahead, Célia.
She tries to turn, intending to buy Célia a few more seconds to escape, but the roar of an engine drowns out even the beast's howl.

items.speaker: Driver
items.text: Get in!

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: You! Wait, shouldn't you be in the hospital?

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Ah, you can explain later. Célia, get in the car!
She yanks the car door open, shoves the dazed Célia inside, then jumps into the back seat.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Go! Go! Hit the gas!
